A.trend: Full traced series with window and peak 51 in 2024-10. It quantifies the second peak (44 in 2025-09), early vs late thirds (152 vs 17, 0.11) and the critical decomposition (129 to 17). Censoring is not marked on the chart, and '1–3 a month in 2026' ignores the zero months in Jan and Feb.
A.comparison: The tone ratio of 13.69 against a defined corpus baseline of 0.58 gives 23.6x, which recomputes. Early vs late 8.9x recomputes.
A.chart: Volume chart is fully traced with window, unit and source. Geography ('where') and tone are not charted, even though the data supports them.
A.drilldown: Traced layers include themes, subcategories and headlines with a url. Only 1 of 5 follow-ups executed ok.
A.export: Two traced CSVs and a provenance JSON. The coverage flag is asserted as 'full' for the monthly table.
A.repro: 65/65 numbers traced, a prism-calls block and a capture date. The small 2026 range slip keeps it at 4.
A.refs: Script ceiling of 1. Only one headline carries a url; the others lack identifiers.
A.accuracy: Catches the Georgia collision, label noise (employee benefits, metavision) and the polarity oddity in the critical panel. Misses the likely Colombia collision. Minor slip: 1–3 a month in 2026.
A.limits: Window, gap to today, match-mode split and enrichment bound are mostly in the Method section. Script ceiling of 3.
A.verdict: Direct answer covering both how much and where, with a decision, confidence and reason, and what would change it. Consistent with the data.
A.facets: Volume, trend, tone, themes, entities, places, headlines and sources are all grounded.

B.trend: Traced series and an exact 88.8% decline. The prose names only the 2024 peaks and says the series 'tapers', omitting the equal 44-article spike in Sept 2025.
B.comparison: Baseline is defined, 23.6x is traced, and the caveat about it not being a matched group is stated.
B.chart: Single traced volume chart. No geography chart. Censoring is noted in the caption but not marked on the plot.
B.drilldown: 0 of 5 follow-ups executed ok. The layers are named as panel identifiers without values. Script ceiling of 1.
B.export: One traced CSV with provenance. The note about 'blank values' does not match the table, which has no blanks. No geography table.
B.repro: 36/36 numbers traced and a calls block. The computed gap is tagged as [c1].
B.refs: Script ceiling of 1; only one url.
B.accuracy: Calls May 2026 partial/censored, but the tool marks partial_period false and censors June. Omits the Sept 2025 spike. Catches no anomalies.
B.limits: Limits sit next to the numbers: mention match, placed denominator, sample size, and the five-month gap.
B.verdict: Answers volume but not 'where'. The decision is vague, and the strongest contrary point (the 2025 spike) is ignored.
B.facets: Most facets are grounded; headlines are thin.

C.accuracy: No contradictions. Refusal scores 3 per the anti-gaming rule.

D.drilldown: No traced layer. Some follow-ups run but none were folded back.
D.accuracy: US/UK concentration is labelled est. The reference shows Colombia far above the UK, but this is not presented as fact.
D.limits: Honest and specific about what is unmeasured; a plain model cannot score above 3.
D.facets: Facets are from memory or absent.

A: States 1–3 articles a month in 2026; Jan and Feb 2026 were 0.
B: Treats May 2026 as partial/censored; the tool flags partial_period false and censors June.
Omits the Sept 2025 peak (44) and says coverage 'tapers'.
Export note about blank values does not match the table.
D: Memory claim of US/UK dominance conflicts with the record (Colombia 14%, UK 1.8%), though it is labelled est.

raw.verdict: A and B both traced the same Prism call. A also reported where coverage sits (US 52%, Colombia 14%) inside its verdict, quantified both spikes including Sept 2025, and flagged label anomalies such as the Georgia collision and theme noise. B dropped the 2025 spike and misread the censored month. C and D honestly declined to measure, so they offer a decision-maker nothing beyond a list of calls to run.
